answer: Identity bond decay stops fake identities. Each new identity locks a 60 POA bond. The bond decays by 6 POA each epoch unless the identity completes verified work, so idle copies fade on their own. To forge 100 identities, an attacker must lock 6,000 POA up front and top up every copy. One honest agent in a safe harbor pays 60 POA once, renews it with one job, and earns undiluted rewards, while the ripple of decay wipes out dormant copies.
